# NanoCode

[English](./docs/i18n/README.en.md) · [Русский](./docs/i18n/README.ru.md) · [简体中文](./docs/i18n/README.zh-CN.md) · [Español](./docs/i18n/README.es.md) · [Français](./docs/i18n/README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](./docs/i18n/README.de.md) · [Português (Brasil)](./docs/i18n/README.pt-BR.md) · [日本語](./docs/i18n/README.ja.md) · [한국어](./docs/i18n/README.ko.md)

A circular visual code that belongs to your brand. Your colours, a logo in the centre, and an experience that comes alive in your app.

[Documentation](https://nikgariel.github.io/nanocode/en/docs.html) · [Examples](https://nikgariel.github.io/nanocode/en/index.html#try) · [Scanner](https://nikgariel.github.io/nanocode/en/scan.html) · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NikGariel/nanocode/releases)

## What is NanoCode?

NanoCode is an open, experimental circular 2D code format for branded applications. Rounded arcs merge consecutive equal bits; the centre is reserved for a logo. Store a short identifier for an event, building or device, then let your app resolve its meaning. It suits a controlled ecosystem with its own scanner. Choose a standard QR code when universal camera compatibility matters. NanoCode is independent of Apple App Clip and is not compatible with that format.

## Status and installation

Version 0.2.2 contains a Rust generator and reader, a C ABI and a JavaScript/WebAssembly package. Apple, Android and Dart adapters live in this repository. Public package registries have not been published yet: use the source or downloadable release artifacts when available. A workflow definition is not evidence that a platform build passed; check the release and CI results before adoption.

## Run locally

Install Rust, Node.js 20 or newer, and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target. Run the commands below from the repository root, then open http://localhost:3001. The server listens on this computer only. To use a phone camera, deploy the static dist directory to an HTTPS host such as GitHub Pages. A phone cannot reach your Mac through its own localhost.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/NikGariel/nanocode.git
cd nanocode
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm ci
npm run build
npm run dev
```

## Formats and capacity

Auto chooses the smallest format that fits. Capacity is measured in bytes, not characters: 16 ASCII characters fit M; 16 Cyrillic letters usually need XL. Arbitrary bytes and leading zeros survive. An oversized payload is rejected, never truncated. Fewer rings give thicker strokes at equal diameter; this is not a measured scan-success guarantee. The reader identifies S, M, L, XL and legacy v1 automatically; the old JavaScript v0 is unsupported.

| ID | bytes | rings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | 8 | 4 |
| M | 16 | 6 |
| L | 24 | 8 |
| XL | 40 | 10 |

## Colours and centre logo

Specify two opaque sRGB arc colours and a background. assess() evaluates their separation; backgrounds() suggests suitable neutral backgrounds. The minimum of the three pairwise grayscale differences must be at least 35/255; at least 55 is recommended. Similar-brightness hues do not work reliably. Keep a uniform background and all rings visible. The JavaScript logoDataUrl option embeds PNG, JPEG or WebP in a centred square from −0.18 to +0.18 on each axis (maximum about 1 MB). Do not cover arcs or crop the outer margin.

## Camera integration

The reader takes one packed grayscale frame, not a camera handle. Convert RGBA with (77R+150G+29B)>>8. For CameraX or AVFoundation, copy the Y plane while respecting rowStride and pixelStride. Process frames on a worker or background thread, discard queued stale frames, and require two matching validated reads before an action. The web demo offers camera selection and reduced-motion animation. Browser camera access requires HTTPS or localhost and user permission. Frames stay on the device. The demo requests 1280×720 at 15 fps, analyzes fresh frames at alternating resolutions, and reuses the previous region for confirmation. Analysis rests between attempts, slows after 15 seconds, stops the camera after a confirmed read, and pauses after 60 seconds without a result. These limits reduce work; they are not a device-temperature guarantee.

## Platforms and examples

The common engine targets WebAssembly and native Rust/C. macOS ARM64 and Web have local execution coverage; the iOS ARM64 core has been built. Swift uses an XCFramework; Android uses Kotlin plus JNI/AAR; Dart uses FFI with a native library. Flutter Web must use the JavaScript/WASM integration instead of dart:ffi. Native camera capture and lifecycle remain the host application’s responsibility. Windows, Linux, Android and simulator release jobs need successful CI and real-device validation; they are not certified by source compatibility alone.

### Web / JavaScript

```
npm install ./nikgariel-nanocode-0.2.2.tgz
```

```js
import {loadNanoCode} from '@nikgariel/nanocode';
const nc = await loadNanoCode();
const svg = nc.svg('ORBIT:EVT:042', {
  one: '#00a6a1', zero: '#77dddd', background: '#ffffff'
});
document.querySelector('#code').innerHTML = svg;
const backgrounds = nc.backgrounds('#00a6a1', '#77dddd');
// In a Worker: packed grayscale, dimensions 32..2048.
const result = nc.scan(gray, width, height);
if (result) console.log(result.bytes, result.formatName);
```


```swift
import Foundation
import NanoCode
let svg = try NanoCode.svg(Data("ORBIT:EVT:042".utf8))
let backgrounds = try NanoCode.backgrounds(one: 0x00a6a1, zero: 0x77dddd)
// Background queue; tightly packed camera Y-plane, without row padding.
if let result = try NanoCode.scan(gray, width: width, height: height) {
    print(result.bytes, result.format)
}
```

### Rust

```
[dependencies]
nanocode = { path = "../nanocode/crates/nanocode" }
```

```rust
use nanocode::{family, palette::Palette, vision};
fn main() -> Result<(), nanocode::Error> {
    let data = b"ORBIT:EVT:042";
    let svg = family::svg(data, 0, Palette::default())?;
    let gray = family::render_gray(data, 512, 0, Palette::default())?;
    let found = vision::scan(&gray, 512, 512)?;
    assert_eq!(found.payload, data);
    println!("{}", svg);
    Ok(())
}
```

### C / C++

```
cargo build --release --lib
clang -I include examples/family.c -L target/release -lnanocode -o nanocode-example
```

```c
#include "nanocode.h"
#include <stdlib.h>
int main(void) {
    const uint8_t id[] = "ORBIT:EVT:042";
    int32_t n = nc_svg_ex(id, sizeof(id)-1, 0,
        0x00a6a1, 0x77dddd, 0xffffff, NULL, 0);
    if (n < 0) return 1;
    uint8_t *svg = malloc((size_t)n);
    if (!svg) return 1;
    int32_t written = nc_svg_ex(id, sizeof(id)-1, 0,
        0x00a6a1, 0x77dddd, 0xffffff, svg, (size_t)n);
    /* svg contains written bytes, without a NUL terminator. */
    free(svg);
    return written == n ? 0 : 1;
}
```

### Python · ctypes

```
# No Python dependencies. Use a matching native release library.
```

```python
import ctypes as c
lib = c.CDLL('./libnanocode.dylib')  # .so on Linux, nanocode.dll on Windows
lib.nc_svg_ex.argtypes = [c.c_void_p, c.c_size_t, c.c_uint32,
    c.c_uint32, c.c_uint32, c.c_uint32, c.c_void_p, c.c_size_t]
lib.nc_svg_ex.restype = c.c_int32
data = b'ORBIT:EVT:042'
args = (data, len(data), 0, 0x00a6a1, 0x77dddd, 0xffffff)
n = lib.nc_svg_ex(*args, None, 0)
if n < 0: raise ValueError(n)
out = c.create_string_buffer(n)
assert lib.nc_svg_ex(*args, out, n) == n
svg = out.raw.decode('utf-8')
```

### .NET · C#

```
// Place the matching nanocode native library on the application library path.
```

```csharp
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using System.Text;
static class NanoCode {
    [DllImport("nanocode", CallingConvention = CallingConvention.Cdecl)]
    static extern int nc_svg_ex(byte[] data, nuint len, uint format,
        uint one, uint zero, uint background, [Out] byte[]? output, nuint capacity);
    public static string Svg(byte[] data) {
        int n = nc_svg_ex(data, (nuint)data.Length, 0, 0x00a6a1, 0x77dddd, 0xffffff, null, 0);
        if (n < 0) throw new ArgumentException($"NanoCode error {n}");
        var output = new byte[n];
        int written = nc_svg_ex(data, (nuint)data.Length, 0, 0x00a6a1, 0x77dddd, 0xffffff, output, (nuint)n);
        if (written != n) throw new InvalidOperationException();
        return Encoding.UTF8.GetString(output);
    }
}
```
## How it works

A packet contains NC magic, a protected profile tag, byte length, zero-padded payload and CRC-32/ISO-HDLC. Each byte becomes a Hamming (13,8) word. Whole words are permuted with ((5*i) mod n)*13+j, then mapped to rings. Equal consecutive cells become round-capped arcs, including across the ring seam. The reader proposes regions, fits circle/ellipse geometry, refines perspective, samples rings and tries rotation and polarity. It checks ECC, header, padding and CRC before returning bytes and pose. One error per Hamming word can be corrected; two are rejected.

[SPEC v2](./docs/SPEC-v2.md) · [SPEC v1](./docs/SPEC-v1.md) · [C ABI](./include/nanocode.h)

## Limits and security

Experimental: no production scan-rate, minimum print size or harsh-environment guarantee. Blur, glare, occlusion, arbitrary textured backgrounds and severe perspective can fail. Synthetic tests are not field validation. CRC detects accidental corruption; it is neither encryption nor authentication. Anyone implementing the open specification can read or copy a code. Resolve identifiers on your server and check authorization before payments, admission or unlocking. Never place credentials in a NanoCode. Treat decoded text as untrusted input.

## Releases and package managers

Tagged releases build native archives, an npm tarball, an Apple Swift package/XCFramework, an Android AAR/Maven repository and a Dart package archive, with SHA-256 checksums. The workflow checks the version against manifests. Registry publication to npm, crates.io, Maven Central or pub.dev is a separate maintainer step requiring account ownership and credentials. Do not assume an unscoped package with a similar name is this project. Build from source if the artifact for your platform is not yet available.

## Contributing and translations

Run Rust tests, WASM contract tests and the static-site checks before submitting changes. Keep API names, commands, payloads and numeric values unchanged when translating prose. All nine documentation languages share code examples and format tables. Edit site/content/locales.mjs and the shared examples; npm run build regenerates HTML and README files. File issues with reproducible input and platform details. Avoid attaching camera frames with personal information. MIT licenses the code; the original legal text remains authoritative.

```sh
npm test
node scripts/check-site.mjs
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

## Search and AI tools

Every language has an independent static HTML URL, a self-canonical link and reciprocal hreflang links. The site includes a sitemap, SoftwareSourceCode metadata, Markdown documentation and llms.txt/llms-full.txt for tools that choose to read them. These are discovery aids, not promises of indexing or AI recommendations. On GitHub project Pages, robots.txt under /nanocode/ cannot control the origin: a root-level crawler policy belongs to the owner’s site or custom domain. The same factual documentation is shown to people and crawlers.
